sources.note: Demand origin and standard boundary explanation.

statement: A demand zone originates from the final bearish candle before the approved bullish departure.

sources.note: Supply origin and standard boundary explanation.

statement: A supply zone originates from the final bullish candle before the approved bearish departure.

sources.note: Standard supply bounds.
Standard demand bounds.

statement: Standard zone geometry uses the approved origin candle range unless an accuracy-zone condition applies or the formation envelope extends the distal bound.

sources.note: Accuracy demand condition and body-based proximal bound.
Protected-indicator parity on Vantage USDJPY five-minute data showed the accuracy-demand proximal edge at the origin body while the distal edge retained the lower origin wick.

statement: When the bearish demand origin extends above the first bullish departure, use the origin body high for the proximal accuracy boundary, retain the origin low for the distal boundary, and allow formation lows to extend that distal boundary farther before confirmation.

sources.note: Accuracy supply condition.
Accuracy supply body-based proximal bound.

statement: When the bullish supply origin extends below the first bearish departure, use the origin body low for the proximal accuracy boundary, retain the origin high for the distal boundary, and allow formation highs to extend that distal boundary farther before confirmation.

sources.note: Fresh and untapped zone requirement.

statement: A tradable zone must remain fresh; a disallowed return after confirmation changes its lifecycle state and it is no longer an untapped setup.

sources.note: Same-direction departure wick exception during formation.

statement: A same-direction departure candle wick that overlaps the forming zone is formation evidence and does not count as a post-confirmation tap.

sources.note: User clarified that the bullish departure wick below the bearish origin must be included in the demand zone before confirmation.

statement: Before demand confirmation, consecutive bullish formation candles may extend only the distal boundary downward with their lows; the boundary freezes at confirmation.

sources.note: Approved closed-bar detector contract derived from the canonical RD examples.

statement: Confirm demand only when a bullish five-minute candle closes above the origin high, and confirm supply only when a bearish five-minute candle closes below the origin low.

sources.note: Approved supply-side mirror of the user-confirmed demand formation-wick rule.

statement: Before supply confirmation, consecutive bearish formation candles may extend only the distal boundary upward with their highs; the boundary freezes at confirmation.

sources.note: Approved deterministic reversal/continuation classification contract.

Protected-indicator parity on Vantage GBPJPY five-minute data: the 00:50 demand origin followed a 00:45 doji, so classification used the nearest earlier directional 00:40 bullish candle and retained the zone confirmed at 01:00.

statement: Classify a zone from the nearest directional candle within 20 bars before the origin, skipping intervening dojis: continuation when that approach matches the departure direction, otherwise reversal. Reject only when no directional approach exists in the bounded lookback.

sources.note: Approved deterministic handling of an opposite candle before confirmation.

statement: After departure formation starts, an opposite-color candle before confirmation rejects that candidate unless the confirmed inside-base rebase exception applies.

sources.note: Protected-indicator parity on Vantage GBPJPY five-minute data: the contained 04:50 bearish candle replaced the 04:40 demand origin, and the protected distal boundary started at the rebased origin low 218.386 instead of retaining the pre-rebase 04:45 bullish wick at 218.362.

Protected-indicator visual parity case on Vantage USDJPY five-minute data: after a contained bearish candle rebased the accuracy-demand origin, its own lower wick extended the protected distal edge below the later bullish departure wick.

statement: When an opposite-color candle appears after formation starts but remains fully inside the prior origin range, rebase the candidate to that candle, restart the distal formation envelope at the rebasing candle low for demand or high for supply, discard pre-rebase departure wicks, and wait for a new same-direction departure; otherwise reject the interruption.

sources.note: Approved non-repainting zone lifecycle contract.

statement: Freeze top and bottom at the confirmation close; later bars may change lifecycle state or right-edge projection but never resize the price bounds.

sources.note: Approved lifecycle policy separating a tap from a close through the distal boundary.

statement: After confirmation, an overlap is a tap unless the closed candle finishes beyond the distal boundary, which invalidates the zone.

sources.note: Approved deterministic runtime contract for the scalping detector.

statement: Evaluate and emit detector decisions only on confirmed bars of a five-minute chart.

sources.note: Latest RD Forex course requires at least two opposite-direction candle closes for valid liquidity in front of an already identified zone.
RD Forex full guide states that two candles are the minimum for normal liquidity trades and one candle alone does not form structure.

statement: After raw zone confirmation and before its first tap, normal demand liquidity requires a run of at least two consecutive bearish five-minute candles and normal supply liquidity requires a run of at least two consecutive bullish five-minute candles.

sources.note: Latest RD Forex course defines the universal own-extreme requirement and identifies the high or low point made before forming liquidity as the level that must be taken.

statement: For a completed liquidity run, use the starting swing's wick extreme as its own extreme: the maximum high of the immediately preceding bar and bearish run for demand, or the minimum low of the immediately preceding bar and bullish run for supply. A later closed bar must trade strictly beyond that level before the still-fresh zone is strategy-eligible.

sources.note: Latest RD Forex course calls the liquidity closest to the zone the main one and describes additional independently swept swings as extra confidence.

statement: When several completed liquidity swings exist before the first zone tap, the main candidate is the one spatially closest to the zone: the lowest swing low above demand or the highest swing high below supply. That primary candidate must have taken its own extreme; older swept candidates are supporting confidence and cannot keep the setup eligible while a closer completed primary remains unswept.

sources.note: RD Forex permits one-candle liquidity only with a large retracement, a fakeout at an obvious normal zone, and clear direction; the qualitative thresholds are not objective.
RD Forex edge example reiterates that one-candle liquidity needs an obvious zone and stronger caution.

statement: One-candle liquidity is a discretionary exception requiring a large retracement, an obvious normal supply-or-demand fakeout, and clear direction; until those qualitative terms have objective thresholds, automation must reject it by default.

sources.note: After liquidity is taken, RD Forex rejects a setup when price retraces into an intervening normal opposite zone and then returns toward the target; a slight retracement without that structure remains acceptable.

statement: After a target zone becomes liquidity-eligible, expire the setup when a later closed five-minute bar taps a confirmed opposite-direction raw zone located fully in front of the still-fresh target. Do not reject a route for a slight retracement alone, and do not treat an invalidated opposite zone as this blocker.

sources.note: RD Forex rejects a target tap before liquidity takes its own extreme and accepts the later target tap when liquidity was taken first, including a short period of price hanging around before the return.

statement: A non-executable setup may arm only after qualifying liquidity takes its own extreme while the target remains fresh. Its first later target overlap is a valid setup return unless the bar invalidates the target; a target overlap before or on the same closed five-minute bar as eligibility is rejected because ordering is unproven.
